Let me evaluate each option.

Root question: whether molecular mapping of AAAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determines which variants transcytose vs remain intracellular, and which binding signatures.

Option 1: Structural coverage of capsid–receptor–glycan complexes. Subject: computed structural coverage of capsid-receptor complexes — same subject (capsid-receptor binding signatures), asks whether epitope geometry/kinetics can be computed. It asks the "for which binding signatures" half — arguably SAME (sub-question: which signatures). I'd say SAME.

Stakes: if answered, whether computed coverage recovers signatures accurately enough — would turn on choices: whether to compute or measure per complex.4-5. I'll say 4? The criteria: 5 = choice someone faces turns on answer. Choosing compute vs experiment — yes, that's a build/collect choice. 5.

Open: names quantity (model runs per pH), where published work stops (5 models, 20 recycles), unmeasured range starts within $1000 reach? AlphaFold-Multimer runs are cheap; yes. 5.

Reshape: names chain 10^9-10^12 steps, one replica fills GPU (fails criterion — one replica keeps GPU busy, so copies side by side... actually one run fills GPU, which per rubric is a "3" fail condition). Also names condition for parallel (decorrelation of replicas, checkable via timescale separation), and adaptive sampling source scaled linearly to 5000 parallel sims — a cited source already computes this chain in parallel for MD generally (different system? it's protein folding, not this system — "A method published for a different system does not lower this score"). But one replica fills a GPU → 3.

Option 2: Sequence-to-function ML. Root link: classifier on binding features for BBB transport — subject is capsid variants + transcytosis, but the question is whether classifier can be accurate. It's ADJACENT (has root's subject — AAV variants/transcytosis prediction — but asks different question: classifier accuracy, not receptor binding signatures). Hmm, root asks: can molecular mapping of receptor interactions determine which variants transcytose. This asks whether sequence-to-function ML can be made accurate — different approach/question. ADJACENT.

Stakes: whether to invest in more labels for classifier vs binding map — choice turns. 4. Actually if answered, would it change choice about library design/training? Yes, moderately. 4.

Open: names quantity (training set size), where published stop (24K), unknown above whether transcytosis labels lower false-positive rate. $1000 reach: training models on tens of thousands variants — cheap enough. 5.

Reshape: "none" — no sequential chain named; only independent pieces → 1.

Option 3: In-silico search of insert space. Subject: enumerating candidate inserts in silico. ADJACENT or SAME? It bears on domain of signature→fate function; asks whether signatures can be enumerated in silico. Different question from root (root: does molecular mapping determine transcytosis). ADJACENT.

Stakes: compute_open says "settled" — more scoring known to change design yield, already published. So answer already known → 1? The question "whether the domain can be enumerated in silico before any capsid is made" — the cited work already did it. Either answer already expected → 1. Also open: "settled" — published work covers → 1.

Reshape: none, independent scoring → 1.

Option 4: Stochastic simulation of post-endocytic sorting. Subject: post-endocytic sorting fate decision — root mentions "transcytose versus remain intracellular" so subject overlaps (fate of cargo), but the root's object of study is capsid-receptor binding mapping on endothelial cells; this targets sorting instead of binding. Root link says "Bears on the transcytose versus retain outcome itself." I'd say SAME — it asks the outcome half of the root question. Actually the root question is about determining transcytosis vs intracellular retention via binding mapping; this option asks whether sorting simulation predicts that label. It's a sub-question of the root (mechanism of transcytose vs intracellular fate). SAME.

Stakes: if answered, whether to pursue binding mapping vs sorting simulation — a build/collect choice. 5? Or 4. The answer would change experimental strategy. 5.

Open: names quantity (ensemble members per parameter point), where published stop (many independent sims with std devs), unknown above whether parameterized sims predict real labels. Cheap stochastic sims within reach. 5.

Reshape: names chain (tens to hundreds events per realization), one realization leaves most of GPU idle (good), condition for parallel (decorrelation checkable cheaply), nearest source reports means over independent sims — does a cited source already compute this chain in parallel for this system? The arxiv source does many independent simulations — so parallel ensemble already done for this system. Hmm. "no cited source already computes this chain in parallel for this system" — the arxiv paper did many independent simulations of this sorting process, so ensemble parallelism demonstrated → that fails one criterion. But other elements present. I'd give 3? The rubric: 5 requires all four. Missing "no cited source already computes chain in parallel" → so ≤3. 3.
